subject: a gamepad face-button control-prompt glyph for a game HUD (clean UI iconography)
bestPrompt: A single centered game HUD face-button control-prompt glyph, premium AAA UI iconography in the style of Path of Exile 2, Diablo IV and Hades II. Front-on orthographic view, tightly centered and symmetric. Shape reads instantly: one clean rounded gamepad control key carrying a single hollow triangle symbol at its exact center. Rendered as a physically-lit backlit control key with restrained real material — a smooth dark satin-metal button face (one simple face, no competing concentric rings) with a crisp top rim light and soft ambient occlusion pooling in the lower edge, and a defined three-value light structure. The triangle is a single clean hollow glyph drawn in one even stroke, soft off-white, clearly the brightest element and highest-contrast shape so the eye lands on it first. Crisp intentional edges, high contrast, engineered to stay legible at 40px, controlled soft-contact shadow beneath. Isolated on a plain neutral dark charcoal background, studio product lighting, sharp focus, 8k icon. NOT a flat vector emoji, NOT a gemstone, NOT a glowing bloom, NOT a doubled outline, NOT a smooth sticker, NOT a cel-shaded outline. NO letters, NO numbers, NO words, NO watermark, NO border frame, NO icon grid, NO extra objects, NO glow halo — exactly one clean button glyph.
technique: On Lucid Origin the winning band is a RESTRAINED semi-lit button, not pure flat vector. Three levers: (1) Collapse to exactly ONE dead-center glyph with a hard negative tail (NO text/numbers/watermark/border/grid/extra objects) — this cures the baseline's fatal contact-sheet + garbled-text failure (16→60s) and Lucid renders the clean crisp result well (cleanliness held 88-90 every gen). (2) Use a legible face-button silhouette: rounded control key + one hollow triangle glyph in one even stroke, soft off-white, as the brightest/highest-contrast element so it reads at 40px. (3) Keep material RESTRAINED — a smooth single satin-metal face with ONE top rim light + corner AO + a 3-value structure lifts materialRendering(76)+valueHierarchy(78) together, but adding emboss/specular/gloss/'gentle top light' language backfires on Lucid, producing doubled glyphs, blown hotspots, or bloom-mush (i3=44, i5=47). Avoid gemstones and nested concentric rings — both read as skeuomorphic knobs and drag styleCohesion.

iterations.note: Prior-best recipe ported to Lucid: satin metal button + emerald gemstone triangle. material 70/value 68/clean 88, but judge flagged gemstone as decorative filler and photoreal knob → styleCohesion 55.

Pure flat vector per judge fix (hollow triangle, 2-tone chip, no metal). silhouette 76/clean 80 but materialRendering collapsed to 38 — judge swung back to 'render as a lit 3D control'. Confirms flat undershoots the rubric.
Added emboss/inner-shadow/specular-sweep language → Lucid produced a DOUBLED ghosted glyph (cyan outline offset from grey fill) + blown specular hotspot. edge 45/styleCohesion 40. Reverted.

BEST. i1 recipe with gemstone→neutral hollow off-white triangle and 'one simple face, no competing rings'. value 78/material 76/clean 90/edge 72. Capped by styleCohesion 54 (still reads photoreal knob) + triangle slightly off-center.
Pushed semi-flat single face per fix. Lucid re-introduced glossy-plastic bloom edges + a stray orange hotspot → edge 38. The 'gentle top-down light' phrasing keeps triggering gloss/bloom artifacts.

i4 recipe verbatim + stronger dead-center language. Pure execution variance: disc came out muddy brown with weak value separation vs near-black bg → material 55/value 58. Shows Lucid can't reliably reproduce the i4=61 result.

ceiling: ~61, NOT model-improved over gpt-image-2. Hypothesis only PARTIALLY confirmed: Lucid does render clean crisp edges better (cleanliness 88-90 vs gpt-image-2's lower band), but the judge rubric structurally rewards materialRendering+valueHierarchy, so Lucid's flat-vector default (i2) still undershoots at 55 and lands in the SAME high-50s/low-60s band. 90 is NOT reachable via prompt alone here: the rubric holds an unresolvable conflict for 'flat UI iconography' — styleCohesion penalizes any lit/skeuomorphic button (wants flatter) while materialRendering+valueHierarchy penalize flat fills (want lit 3D), so the best score straddles the middle. Compounded by heavy Lucid per-gen variance (i4=61 vs i6=54 from near-identical prompts: bloom, muddy discs, off-center glyphs). This family is genuinely capped for text-to-image; the real fix is vector/SDF tooling or a rubric that does not demand painterly material of a flat HUD glyph.
